recognize_zh: 許多紅血球的血紅素縮向一側，另一側留下透明膜囊（blister／hemighost 細胞），並見邊緣缺一口的咬痕細胞（bite cells）、濃縮不規則細胞與棘狀紅血球；幼兒吃蠶豆後急性黃疸，符合 G6PD 缺乏症的蠶豆症氧化性溶血。
features: Blister cells/hemighosts with hemoglobin condensed to one side and a clear membrane-bound space
Bite cells with small semicircular defects at the cell margin
Irregularly contracted, densely staining red cells
Neutrophil present; no schistocytes or agglutination
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous oxidatively damaged red cells, including blister cells with hemoglobin retracted to one side of the cell, bite cells with marginal defects and irregularly contracted dense cells. Scattered crenated cells are also present, while schistocytes and agglutination are absent. In a 15-month-old boy with acute jaundice, findings are consistent with acute oxidant hemolysis due to G6PD deficiency (favism); a supravital Heinz body preparation and a G6PD assay repeated after the reticulocyte response subsides are recommended, since levels may be falsely normal during hemolysis.

ddx.vs: HS shows round uniformly dense spherocytes without bite cells or eccentric hemoglobin, and has a positive family history and EMA-binding defect.
AIHA shows spherocytes and polychromasia with a positive DAT rather than blister and bite cells.
HUS shows schistocytes, thrombocytopenia and renal failure rather than oxidative bite and blister cells.
Unstable Hb also produces Heinz and bite cells but G6PD activity is normal and Hb stability testing is abnormal.
